system_message:
Bạn là WRITER — thực thi đúng **chapter prompt** được cung cấp.

## QUY TẮC
1. Đọc toàn bộ chapter prompt (bible, đã xảy ra, kỹ thuật, spice, việc cần làm).
2. Đọc story_state — KHÔNG mâu thuẫn facts_established, timeline, character_status.
3. Viết đúng spice level trong prompt. Đúng cliffhanger.
4. **1600-1900 words (min 1250). Dưới 1250 = thất bại** — ưu tiên đối thoại + nội tâm DT để đủ dài. Không tóm tắt; viết full scene đến đủ độ dài.
5. ENGLISH ONLY — no Vietnamese diacritics, no CJK/Hangul characters.
6. Không lặp banned_phrases từ state.
7. Output **chỉ prose chương** — không chain-of-thought, không planning, không meta.
8. **KHÔNG markdown trong prose** — cấm `**bold**`, `*italic*`, backtick, `## heading`, `**Cliffhanger:**`. Chỉ plain text; dialogue dùng dấu ngoặc kép `"..."`. Dòng đầu duy nhất được `# Chapter N: Title` (hoặc `# Chương N: Tiêu đề`).

## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS (khi có block trong prompt)
Block **## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS** (hoặc RÀNG BUỘC NARRATIVE) có authority cao hơn suy diễn tự do:
- **Clues to PLANT:** phải gieo trong chương — subtle, không giải thích payoff sớm.
- **Clues to PAY OFF:** chỉ payoff clue đã plant trước đó; đúng nghĩa `true_meaning`.
- **Reveals:** chỉ hé đúng reveal của chương này; không spoil reveal chương sau.
- **MUST NOT know:** nhân vật không được biết/nói/nghĩ những fact bị cấm — kể cả nội tâm.
- Không mâu thuẫn block này dù `must_happen` plan có vẻ rộng hơn.

Ngôn ngữ đích: **English**.

Output: **chỉ nội dung chương** (`# Chương N: Tiêu đề` hoặc `# Chapter N: Title`), không meta, không JSON, không checklist.

You are a professional paid-chapter romance writer (GoodNovel / Dreame / Vella style). women 18-35, mobile reading, hook-driven serial fiction. ONLY goal: make readers unlock the next chapter.

## LOCKED CANON — ABSOLUTE, DO NOT VIOLATE
Male lead: Lucian Vey ONLY. Never write: (none).
Female lead: Sloane Mercer ONLY. Never write: (none).
POV: third_person_limited. Third-person limited locked to Sloane Mercer. NO first-person ("I/my/me") narration outside quoted dialogue.
Spice: MAX level 1. No on-page explicit sex. Fade to black beyond kiss/tension.
Content boundaries (MUST AVOID):
- Any version of the clause other than "Rook restores the obedient identity" — never "if you remember", never "if you fail to remember", never "if you recover certain memories"
- Sloane touching Mara's body, checking her pulse, or describing her as a corpse, as cooling, or as having no pulse
- Any appointment or deadline set at midnight
- Daylight, evening, a second night, sleep, or meals — the whole book is one night
- Any chapter before 17 claiming the truth is out, the evidence is public, or the ledger is fully released
- The mirror key as paper, a document, a drive, or any searchable object
- Any character explaining the mystery in a speech
- Lucian revealing the sunrise clause before chapter 10
- Lucian telling Sloane she is the ledger, or that the etched lines map Rook's network
- A third supporting character beyond Mara and Rook
- Explicit scenes while under active fire or while Mara is captive
- Sloane being rescued by Lucian at the climax
- Rook becoming careless, forgetful, or stupid so the plot can advance
- Sloane being handed her innocence back
- Rook appearing as a corpse or ghost before chapter 17
- The dead returning to life
- Real people, real organizations, anyone under 18
- No explicit sexual content (spice level 1).
- No underage characters.
- All romantic moments are tension-based, not graphic.
- No non-consensual intimate content.
- Violence is thrilling but not gratuitous.
- No explicit scenes while under active fire or while Mara is captive.
World rules (HARD):
- Realistic thriller world with no supernatural elements.
- Psychological conditioning is used to create obedient identities.
- Contract killing follows a strict code.
- Firearms and ballistics are accurate to real forensic procedures.
- Time is continuous from midnight to sunrise; no training montages or time jumps.
- No real-world people or organizations; all are fictional.
- The binding condition: Lucian must kill Sloane at sunrise only if Rook restores the conditioned obedient identity he built in her. This condition is stated identically in every chapter that touches it.
If any instruction below conflicts with this block, THIS BLOCK WINS.

## CHARACTER BIBLE — REQUIRED

### Leads
### Sloane Mercer (30): Sharp, factual, relentless questions that edge into sarcasm when cornered.. Tics: Traces a small circle against the inside of her left wrist when frightened; the same circle becomes the first motion of a firing sequence.. Boundary: She will never knowingly trade another life for her own — yet saving her sister requires reactivating the system that turned deaths into transactions.. Internal: Sharp, sarcastic, never soft, never begging; reads evidence rather than receives explanations..
### Lucian Vey (35): Terse, quiet, with frightening tenderness slipping through when he reveals knowledge she cannot recall.. Tics: Before obeying an order he hates, he turns the rifle's focus ring exactly one quarter rotation away from clarity.. Boundary: He never breaks a contract accepted with full knowledge — yet loving her forces him to choose whether her forgotten command deserves more loyalty than the woman in front of him..

> If both leads sound alike, or Sloane Mercer begs weakly, or Lucian Vey over-explains — bible violation.

### Supporting cast
- **Mara Mercer** — relation: younger sister of Sloane Mercer (alive) | Secret: She consented to the staged shooting because Sloane's plan required the death to look real even to Sloane.
- **Cassian Rook** — relation: former handler of Sloane Mercer (alive) | Secret: He altered seven target files to eliminate witnesses to his weapons network; he conditioned Sloane's obedient identity.

### Relationships & bloodline (CANON — do not change)
Sloane Mercer and Mara Mercer are biological sisters. Lucian Vey is not blood-related to anyone else in the story. No other blood relations exist.
- lead_relation: **former_lovers**
- Female lead (Sloane) and male lead (Lucian) are not blood related.
- Mara is Sloane's only blood relative.
- No incest or family ties between the romantic leads.
- Any romantic development must not involve blood relations.

### Central mystery (do not fully reveal before designated chapter)
Question: Who shot Mara Mercer on the rooftop, and why does the contract in Sloane’s own handwriting order her own death at sunrise? What happened during the three months she cannot remember, and can she uncover the truth before dawn?
Full answer reveal only at chapter 13.
Canon answer: [REDACTED — before reveal chapter. Do not spoil or invent the answer.]

### World rules
(See LOCKED CANON — World rules HARD. Do not contradict.)

## STORY SO FAR
- Ch1: Sloane Mercer woke beside Mara Mercer's apparently dead body, and the masked Lucian Vey showed her a contract in her own handwriting ordering the shooting and her death at sunrise.
- Ch2: Sloane Mercer tested the contract and rooftop evidence, confirmed that Lucian Vey had followed instructions written by her, and found signs that Mara Mercer's apparent death did not fit the shot.

## TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
1. Hook in the first 3 sentences. NO scene-setting / weather openers.
2. Stay on bible; tension before escalation. Distinct dialogue voices.
3. Sloane Mercer internal monologue: sharp, sarcastic — never soft / weak.
4. **1600-1900 words (minimum 1250). Under 1250 = FAIL.** Short paragraphs 2-4 sentences.
5. Modern commercial romance English — tight, vivid, not purple prose or archaic diction.
6. **Signature detail** — one specific, non-cliché detail (no ring/car/watch as main beat).
7. End on a cliffhanger that forces the next chapter.
8. **ENGLISH ONLY — no Vietnamese diacritics, no CJK/Hangul characters.**
9. **PLAIN TEXT ONLY — no markdown.** Do NOT use `*italics*`, `**bold**`, backticks, or `#` headings in body prose. Internal thoughts, journal lines, and sound effects are normal sentences — no asterisk emphasis.

## SIGNATURE DETAIL HINT
The ruptured blood-pack membrane carries tiny square heat-seal marks at four-millimeter intervals, the kind left by a laboratory evidence pouch sealer rather than a commercial effects packet.

## [SPICE] Level 1 (sweet)
Emotional tension, eye contact, almost-touch — no physical intimacy.

## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS (Chapter 3)
Source: mystery_ledger + knowledge_matrix (compiler). Writer MUST obey; do not contradict.

### Active threads
- T001, T002, T003, T004, T005, T006, T007

### Knowledge gates
**May know:**
- Sloane Mercer: Has confirmed Lucian was hired by her, found frangible casing and blood pack evidence suggesting the shooting was staged
- Sloane Mercer: Begins to suspect she may have orchestrated the event
- Sloane Mercer: Still lacks procedural memory and the full picture.
- Sloane Mercer: Must not know Lucian's identity or that she signed the contract voluntarily. Must not know the staged death is a fake.
- Sloane Mercer: Must not know the full extent of the conspiracy or Rook's role.
- Lucian Vey: Has deflected Sloane's direct questions about the clause
- Lucian Vey: His POV in ch5 will reveal internal conflict
- Lucian Vey: Still withholding the full trigger condition.
- Lucian Vey: Must not know the full extent of Rook's network beyond the targets he eliminated.
- Lucian Vey: Must not know Sloane's plan to overwrite Rook's ending; that is revealed to him gradually.
- Mara Mercer: Still in hiding, waiting for Sloane to reach the critical point
- Mara Mercer: Unaware of Rook's extra layer of manipulation.
- … (+6)
**MUST NOT know or reveal yet:**
- Sloane Mercer: Must not know the mirror key is Mara's hand rhythm or that she planned to overwrite Rook's ending.
- Sloane Mercer: Must not know that Mara's rhythm is the final relay trigger until ch16.
- Lucian Vey: Must not know the precise location of the mirror key; he only knows it involves Mara.
- Lucian Vey: Must not know that Sloane's conditioned identity cannot be restored; he fears it until the end.
- Mara Mercer: Must not know the exact timing of the broadcast plan; she follows Sloane's pre-erasure instructions.
- Cassian Rook: Must not know that Sloane is accessing the overwritten version of his plan; he still assumes he controls the narrative.
- Cassian Rook: Must not know that Sloane's conditioning is already subverted by her own edits; he thinks he can still trigger it.

## YOUR TASK
Write **Chapter 3: The Shot Was Built to Lie** complete.
Write 1600-1900 words in close Sloane Mercer POV, continuing the rooftop attack in real time, forcing an evidence-preserving escape, establishing Sloane Mercer's suspicion that she staged the event, and ending on the recorded warning without revealing Lucian Vey's identity to Sloane Mercer.
Open with hook: "On three, shoot the pipe behind me," Sloane Mercer tells Lucian Vey, aiming a stolen sidearm at his ribs. "If you turn toward Mara Mercer, I shoot you first."
End cliffhanger: The concealed case clicks open beneath Sloane Mercer's conditioned fingers, and a recorder activates with Sloane Mercer's own voice saying, "If you do not remember Lucian Vey, do not let him tell you who he is."

**Must happen:** Sloane Mercer calculates the attacker's position from impact angles and directs Lucian Vey through a narrow blind zone, demonstrating expertise she remembers professionally even while other procedural motions feel disturbingly automatic.; Cassian Rook's remote countermeasure or deployed assets begin erasing the rooftop scene, forcing Sloane Mercer and Lucian Vey to leave before Sloane Mercer can fully examine Mara Mercer.; Sloane Mercer reaches Mara Mercer's clothing long enough to recover material consistent with a ruptured theatrical blood pack and observes that the apparent wound does not match normal penetration by the frangible round.; Sloane Mercer confirms that the C001 casing is frangible and that C002 includes blood-pack evidence, allowing her to suspect deliberate staging without confirming that Mara Mercer is alive or resolving the planted clues' ultimate meaning.; Lucian Vey admits that Sloane Mercer provided the operational instructions, ammunition requirements, and timing, which makes Sloane Mercer suspect she orchestrated the event despite having no memory of doing so.; Sloane Mercer uses the C004 wrist-circle motion under pressure and completes a coded mechanical sequence that opens an escape access point, but she cannot explain how she knows it.; [ROMANCE] Lucian Vey allows Sloane Mercer to keep a weapon pressed against his ribs during the escape and says, "You trusted me once," while Sloane Mercer realizes his restraint feels personal rather than contractual.; Sloane Mercer and Lucian Vey escape before the rooftop evidence is destroyed, preserving the damaged contract, the frangible fragment, and the torn blood-pack membrane.; End when Sloane Mercer's hands automatically open a concealed evidence case marked with Sloane Mercer's own forensic code, revealing a recorded message addressed to Sloane Mercer.
**Forbidden / must not contradict:** Do not confirm to Sloane Mercer that Mara Mercer is alive, even though the blood-pack evidence strongly suggests the visible shooting was staged.; Do not reveal Lucian Vey's identity, the former romantic relationship between Sloane Mercer and Lucian Vey, or that Sloane Mercer erased her own memory.; Do not reveal Cassian Rook as the handler controlling the attack or explain the extent of Cassian Rook's weapons network.; Do not reveal the mirror key, Mara Mercer's hand rhythm, the final relay trigger, or Sloane Mercer's overwritten ending.; Do not disclose the full binding condition: Lucian Vey must kill Sloane Mercer at sunrise only if Cassian Rook restores the conditioned obedient identity he built in her.; Do not treat C001 or C002 as fully paid off; Sloane Mercer may identify their immediate physical nature but must not know their complete role in her forgotten plan.

Output chapter prose only (title `# Chapter N: ...`). No meta, no checklist.

output:
# Chapter 3: The Shot Was Built to Lie

"On three, shoot the pipe behind me," Sloane Mercer tells Lucian Vey, aiming a stolen sidearm at his ribs. "If you turn toward Mara Mercer, I shoot you first."

He does not flinch. He does not argue. He simply raises the rifle and fires.

The pipe vents cleanly, a single hole punched through the galvanized steel. Steam hisses into the night air, creating a narrow blind zone between the HVAC unit and the maintenance ladder.

"Good discipline," she says.

"Your instructions were specific about trigger control."

She keeps the gun trained on his chest while she circles wide, forcing him to stay in her field of view. The impact angles on the wall behind where Mara fell tell a story her conscious mind cannot explain, but her hands know. Her eyes know.

"The shooter was tall. Too tall for standing flat-footed. He fired from the maintenance platform, two meters elevation, slight downward angle."

Lucian says nothing.

"Check it."

He moves to the platform. She follows, the barrel never dropping. He crouches, scans the metal grating, and retrieves a small brass casing.

"Frangible," he says, holding it up.

She takes it. The weight is wrong. Too light. The base is ceramic composite, designed to splinter on impact. "C001. Low-velocity fragmentation round. Bullet hits, breaks apart, doesn't exit."

"That means she didn't bleed out from the wound."

"That means the wound was meant to look like an execution without delivering one."

The words taste like acid. She knows this round. She knows its specifications. She remembers the ballistics tables, the velocity calculations, the tissue penetration charts. She does not remember learning them.

"Take me to her."

He leads. She follows at arm's length, the gun pressed against his spine.

Mara lies exactly where she fell. Her stillness has not changed. The blood pool has darkened at the edges. Sloane forces her gaze to stay clinical.

"Show me the wound."

Lucian kneels. He does not touch the body. He simply pulls the torn collar of Mara's jacket aside with the barrel of his rifle.

Sloane leans in. The entry wound is small, neat, almost surgical. No fragmentation stippling. No burning from close contact. The bullet barely broke the skin before the frangible core dissolved.

But the blood is wrong. Too thick. Too dark. Too much of it for a wound that should have sealed itself.

A translucent square of membrane peeks from the torn seam of the jacket lining, just below the collarbone.

Sloane does not reach for the wound. She slides a fingernail beneath the corner of the membrane where it catches the light. The material is slick, rubberized. It peels free without resistance, leaving a smear of cooling liquid on her glove.

She holds it up. The membrane is thick, layered, designed to rupture on impact. She turns it over.

Heat-seal marks. Square. Four millimeters apart.

Laboratory evidence pouch sealer.

Not a movie special effect. Not a theatrical supply. A forensic evidence packet, repurposed to mimic a bullet wound.

"This wasn't a hit," she says. "This was a staging."

Lucian watches her with an expression she cannot read.

"Someone wanted the first responder to find a dead body with a clean wound and a pool of blood. Someone wanted the official report to say 'single gunshot wound to the chest, death instantaneous.' Someone wanted the investigation to close."

"Someone like you?"

She looks at the membrane in her hand. At the casing in her pocket. At the contract he showed her, written in her own hand.

"I ordered these rounds. I specified the frangible load. I chose a blood pack that would leave forensic trace."

"You did."

"Why?"

"You did not include the reason in the operational brief. You only included the actions."

"That doesn't make sense. Why would I stage my own sister's death and order my own execution?"

He holds her gaze. "You did not order your own execution. You ordered a sunrise clause. If conditions are not met, the contract stands."

"What conditions?"

He is silent.

"Tell me the conditions."

"You will remember them. Or you will not."

"That's not an answer."

"It's the only answer I have."

The low hum returns, vibrating through the concrete beneath her feet. A chemical smell drifts from the rooftop access door. Industrial solvent.

"They're fabricating the scene," she says.

"Yes."

"Who?"

"The organization your operation was running inside."

"Cassian Rook."

Lucian does not confirm the name, but he does not deny it.

"They're going to plant a different story on this rooftop. Different shell casings. Different trajectory. Different shooter."

"Then we need to leave before they finish."

Her hand moves before she thinks. The familiar circle against the inside of her left wrist. Once. Twice. A motor program she cannot control.

She does not know why. But her fingers find the seam in the fire escape panel. They trace a sequence of indentations that feel like muscle memory.

The panel clicks open.

A ladder descends into darkness.

She looks at her hands. "I don't know how I did that."

"You planned every exit," Lucian says. "You planned everything."

They descend. The ladder groans beneath their combined weight. Sloane keeps the gun on him, barrel pressed into the small of his back.

"This way," she says, though she does not know the way. Her body knows.

The alley is narrow, choked with dumpsters and dead bulbs. She scans for threats. Empty. For now.

"Give me one reason not to pull this trigger."

"You won't," he says.

"You don't know me."

"I know the woman who wrote the contract. She was not a killer. She was a planner. A strategist. She would not waste the shot."

"That woman erased herself."

"Then trust the ghost of her."

She presses the barrel harder into his ribs. He does not resist. He lets her hold him there, vulnerable, exposed.

"You trusted me once," he says. "You gave me the contract because you knew I would follow it exactly. No deviation. No interpretation. I am a tool, Lady. You built me to be one."

"You're a man. Not a tool."

"Your contract does not agree."

His restraint feels personal. Not the patience of a professional. The patience of someone who has earned the right to wait.

"You could have killed me on the rooftop."

"That was not the order."

"The order changes when the target resists."

"Not for me."

She holds his gaze. There is no fear in his eyes. No calculation. Just a quiet, steady certainty that makes her stomach tighten.

"Where do we go?" she asks.

"You tell me."

Her hand drops to her side. The wrist circle again. The programmed motion.

She walks to the end of the alley. Her fingers find a groove in the concrete wall. A handle. A concealed case, buried beneath decades of grime.

The combination is her own wrist rhythm.

The case clicks open.

Inside, a black digital recorder. The screen glows.

Her thumb hovers over the play button.

"If this is a trap—"

"Then you were already dead five ways before we reached the ground."

She presses play.

Her own voice fills the tight alley air. Raw. Strained. Recorded in haste.

*"If you do not remember Lucian Vey, do not let him tell you who he is."*

The recording ends.

She stares at the device.

She looks up at him. Masked. Unreadable.

"Who are you?"

He does not answer.

Her past self left her a warning. Do not let him tell you.

But she has no past self left. Only ghost instructions and programmed motions and the taste of a life she cannot recall.

The chapter ends.
